modules.h1: Titanium Dioxide REACH Registration: What Procurement Teams Should Verify
modules.body: Understand which EU REACH information matters for titanium dioxide procurement, distinguish substance-level information from supplier-specific evidence, and prepare the context needed to review or request supporting documentation.
modules.scope_line: For procurement teams reviewing supply into the EU/EEA. UK REACH applies separately in Great Britain; Northern Ireland remains subject to EU REACH arrangements.

orientation.label: EU / EEA
orientation.body: Review the substance, legal entity, role and supply arrangement.

orientation.label: GB
orientation.body: UK REACH operates separately in Great Britain.

orientation.label: NI
orientation.body: EU REACH arrangements continue to apply in Northern Ireland.

modules.heading: What Should an EU REACH Document Review Confirm?
modules.body: An EU REACH document review should identify the substance, the relevant legal entity and supply-chain role, the intended EU/EEA market or use, and the source, scope and date of the information reviewed. Public substance-level information does not by itself establish that a specific legal entity or supply arrangement is covered by an applicable registration.

modules.heading: Separate Substance Information From Supplier Coverage
modules.intro: Public substance information and evidence for a particular supply arrangement answer different questions.

items.heading: Substance information
items.body: A public substance entry can help identify regulatory information about a substance. It can support substance identification and provide general regulatory context.

items.heading: Legal-entity and supply-arrangement evidence
items.body: This evidence should identify the relevant legal entity, its role in the supply chain and the scope to which the information applies. A generic substance entry does not answer those entity- and arrangement-specific questions on its own.

items.heading: Commercial Grade identity
items.body: A commercial Grade name identifies a product offering. It is not the registrant or an independent registration record. Include the relevant Grade in a request when it helps connect the procurement review to the product being considered.

modules.heading: Identify the Relevant Legal Actor and Supply-Chain Role
modules.intro: REACH responsibilities depend on the legal entity and its role in the relevant arrangement. Identify the party named in the evidence before deciding what that evidence supports.

roles.heading: Manufacturer
roles.body: Identify the EEA-established entity manufacturing the substance, where that role applies to the arrangement being reviewed.

roles.heading: Importer
roles.body: Identify the EEA-established entity responsible for bringing the substance into the EEA, where that role applies.

roles.heading: Only Representative
roles.body: A manufacturer, formulator or article producer established outside the EEA may appoint an EEA-based Only Representative to fulfil relevant importer obligations under REACH, where applicable.

modules.note: An Only Representative relationship must be assessed for the named entities and supply arrangement involved. Do not assume that a seller, product name or general substance record identifies the registrant or confirms an Only Representative appointment.

modules.heading: Confirm the EU/EEA Scope — and Keep UK REACH Separate

jurisdictions.heading: European Union / EEA
jurisdictions.body: References to EU REACH on this page include the EEA countries where REACH applies: Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.

jurisdictions.heading: Great Britain
jurisdictions.body: UK REACH operates separately in Great Britain. Evidence for EU REACH should not automatically be treated as confirmation under UK REACH.

jurisdictions.heading: Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.body: EU REACH continues to apply in Northern Ireland. Identify the destination and applicable framework before relying on supporting documentation.

modules.note: If a procurement review involves Great Britain, Northern Ireland or more than one destination, identify each destination and the framework relevant to it before relying on supporting documentation.

modules.heading: Use This Buyer Verification Checklist
modules.intro: Use the following questions to prepare an internal review or a documentation request:

items.label: Substance identity
items.body: What substance is referenced by the information?

items.label: Legal entity
items.body: Which entity is named or otherwise covered by the evidence?

items.label: Supply-chain role
items.body: Is the relevant role manufacturer, importer or Only Representative?

items.label: Market and use
items.body: Which EU/EEA destination, intended use and supply arrangement are being assessed?

items.label: Scope
items.body: What does the information cover, and what remains outside its scope?

items.label: Source and date
items.body: When was the official source updated, if stated, and when was it last reviewed for this page?

items.label: Clarification
items.body: Which entity- or arrangement-specific details still need to be confirmed?

modules.threshold_note: Where a one-tonne-per-year figure is relevant, treat it only as a general threshold applied in the appropriate legal-entity and substance context. Applicable exemptions and other REACH conditions must also be considered; the figure alone does not determine whether a specific arrangement is registered or exempt.

modules.heading: How to Request REACH Documentation

steps.heading: Describe the information you need
steps.body: Explain the EU REACH documentation or clarification required for your procurement review.

steps.heading: Add the relevant context
steps.body: Include the product or Grade, intended EU/EEA destination, application or use, and any known legal-entity or supply-chain details.

steps.heading: Review the request
steps.body: Check the information carried into the Request Documents form. You can change or remove buyer-provided context before submitting.

steps.heading: Submit for review
steps.body: Send the request with your contact and business details. Requests are reviewed after submission. We may ask for additional context before the relevant documentation can be assessed.

modules.request_note: Submission does not confirm document availability.

items.question: Is public substance information enough to confirm coverage under an applicable registration?
items.answer: No. Public substance information can support substance identification and general regulatory understanding. It does not, on its own, establish that a specific legal entity or supply arrangement is covered by an applicable registration.

items.question: Which legal entity and supply-chain role should be checked?
items.answer: Identify the EEA-established legal entity relevant to the arrangement and determine whether its applicable role is manufacturer, importer or Only Representative. Do not assume that the commercial supplier or Grade name is the registrant.

items.question: Does EU REACH information also confirm UK REACH coverage?
items.answer: No. UK REACH operates separately in Great Britain, while Northern Ireland remains subject to EU REACH arrangements. Check the destination and applicable framework before relying on the information.

items.question: What information should I include in a REACH document request?
items.answer: Include the product or Grade, intended EU/EEA destination, application or use, and the documentation or clarification required. Add known legal-entity or supply-chain details when they are available. You do not need every detail before starting a request.

items.question: Does submitting a request confirm registration or document availability?
items.answer: No. A request provides context for review. We may ask for clarification before the relevant documentation can be assessed, and submission does not confirm document availability.
